Construction Materials.Cement: OPC (Ordinary Portland Cement) is common for general use. PPC (Portland Pozzolana Cement) is better for plastering and wet areas. SRC is used where sulphate attack is a risk.
Construction Materials.Steel: Fe500 and Fe500D are standard TMT rebars for construction. 'D' stands for ductility, making it better for earthquake-prone zones.
Construction Materials.Bricks: Red clay bricks are traditional. Fly ash bricks are eco-friendly and offer better finish. AAC blocks are lightweight, saving structural cost and providing good insulation.
Construction Materials.Concrete Mix Ratios: M15 (1:2:4) for plain concrete, M20 (1:1.5:3) for standard RCC work (slabs, beams), M25 (1:1:2) for heavy load structures.

Structural Components.Foundation: Isolated footings for normal soil. Raft/Mat foundation for low bearing capacity soil. Pile foundation for deep loose soil or high rises.
Structural Components.Columns and Beams: Columns transfer vertical loads to foundations. Beams transfer horizontal loads to columns. Minimum column size for a single story is usually 9x9 inches with 4 bars of 12mm.
Structural Components.Slabs: Standard slab thickness is 5-6 inches. Main reinforcement runs along the shorter span, distribution bars along the longer span.

Architecture.Planning: Ensure proper ventilation and natural lighting. Orient the building keeping sun path and wind direction in mind.
Architecture.Green Buildings: Use sustainable materials, rainwater harvesting, solar panels, and energy-efficient lighting. Maximize natural light to reduce energy consumption.

Project Management.Cost Estimation: Cost depends on built-up area and finish quality. Basic finish: ~$20/sqft, Standard: ~$30/sqft, Premium: ~$45+/sqft (approximate localized values).
Project Management.Scheduling: Use Gantt charts. Sequence: Excavation -> Foundation -> Plinth -> Columns/Brickwork -> Lintel -> Roof Slab -> Plastering -> Finishing.

Workforce.Roles: Site Engineer oversees execution. Mason does brickwork/plastering. Bar bender ties steel. Helper assists skilled labor.
Workforce.Labour Estimation: Thumb rule: For 1000 sq ft house, roughly 3-4 masons and 4-5 helpers needed per day for structural work.

Safety.PPE: Hard hats (helmets), safety goggles, reflective vests, steel-toed boots, and gloves are mandatory. Safety harnesses required for work above 2 meters.
Safety.Risk Mitigation: Regular site inspections, clear hazard signages, proper scaffolding, and first aid kits on site.

Delay Causes.Common Reasons: Labour shortages, material supply delays, severe weather (heavy rain), design changes midway, and cash flow issues.
